33.0.1 Hotfix Changes
---------------------

* Fixed a crash on startup when logged into a service integration [WizardCM] ([#554](https://github.com/obsproject/obs-browser/pull/554))
* Fixed a crash when logging into the Twitch integration [WizardCM] ([#14072](https://github.com/obsproject/obs-studio/pull/14072))
* Fixed a deadlock when logging into the YouTube integration [WizardCM] ([#556](https://github.com/obsproject/obs-browser/pull/556))
* Fixed a race condition where browser panels could end up with incorrectly sized content [WizardCM] ([#558](https://github.com/obsproject/obs-browser/pull/558))
* Fixed a memory leak when using the image slideshow source [prgmitchell] ([#14078](https://github.com/obsproject/obs-studio/pull/14078))
* Fixed plugins failing to load on Flatpak [FiniteSingularity] ([#14103](https://github.com/obsproject/obs-studio/pull/14103))
* Fixed Plugin Manager not prompting for save after a change until the dialog is re-opened [Warchamp7] ([#14112](https://github.com/obsproject/obs-studio/pull/14112))

33.0 New Features
-----------------

* Updated CEF from 127/6533 to 150/7871 [WizardCM] ([#13900](https://github.com/obsproject/obs-studio/pull/13900))
  + This is a massive update to the underlying framework used for browser sources and docks from the July 2024 release to September 2026
  + All of this work is on the backend and should be invisible to users. Please be sure to report any new weirdness or problems you run into with browser sources!
* Complete overhaul to plugin loading [FiniteSingularity/PatTheMav] ([#13594](https://github.com/obsproject/obs-studio/pull/13594))
  + First-party plugins are now in a new folder named core
  + Third-party plugins have an updated installation location and folder structure
  + Existing third-party plugins will continue to load from the legacy locations until OBS Studio 34.0
  + More information is available in our [knowledge base article](https://obsproject.com/kb/legacy-plugin-locations)
* Improved how source snapping works in the preview [Warchamp7] ([#12298](https://github.com/obsproject/obs-studio/pull/12298))
  + New visual indicator added
  + Sources now snap along the entire axis instead of only when directly touching
  + Sources no longer snap to hidden sources
* Improved behavior of spinboxes for number values [Warchamp7] ([#12337](https://github.com/obsproject/obs-studio/pull/12337))
  + Typing is no longer mysteriously blocked in some situations
  + Numbers are no longer cut off in some situations
  + Values now update only after pressing Enter and Enter does not close the window
  + Holding Shift + Up/Down now advances multiple steps at a time
  + Dragging the cursor inside the input but outside the text itself now works properly
* Enabled NVENC on Arm64 [RytoEX] ([#13827](https://github.com/obsproject/obs-studio/pull/13827))

33.0 Changes
------------

* Added a check for encoders being missing when loading a profile [derrod] ([#11340](https://github.com/obsproject/obs-studio/pull/11340))
* Added support for newest NVIDIA Broadcast SDKs for NVIDIA Audio Effects and Video Effects [pkviet] ([#13838](https://github.com/obsproject/obs-studio/pull/13838))
* Added hotkeys for controlling audio monitoring of a source [Warchamp7] ([#13599](https://github.com/obsproject/obs-studio/pull/13599))
* Changed Safe Mode to not start WebSocket Server [FiniteSingularity/RytoEX] ([#13984](https://github.com/obsproject/obs-studio/pull/13984))
* Fixed issues with groups in Studio Mode [Warchamp7] ([#11092](https://github.com/obsproject/obs-studio/pull/11092))
  + Fixed moving sources inside a group causing them to glitch out in Program
  + Fixed moving sources inside a group showing up live in Program
* Adjusted naming of Window Capture methods on Windows [Penwy] ([#12047](https://github.com/obsproject/obs-studio/pull/12047))
* Improved detection of fullscreen games for Game Capture [Kira-NT] ([#10880](https://github.com/obsproject/obs-studio/pull/10880))

flow-launcher.changelog:
# Release notes

## Bug fixes

- Fixed Firefox bookmark loading when profiles.ini uses different line endings.

- Reduced error log noise by treating missing shortcut descriptions as debug messages instead of errors.

- History results now appear on startup when the “Show History Results in Home Page” option is enabled, even if the home page is turned off.

- Context menus on the home page now open with the right arrow and show up-to-date options.

- Flow will now take keyboard focus on Windows startup (when not hidden), so you can type in the search box right away.

- Fixed an issue that could leave outdated data in settings or other stored files when saving a new version with shorter JSON content.

- Improved shell command handling for quoted paths and multi-word arguments. Command history now properly preserves your original input.

- Quoted commands now run correctly in the Windows CMD shell, and command launching via Windows Terminal is more reliable.

- Improved URL support for browser, file, about:, and data: links. Removed insecure ftp:// support.

- Improved URL matching for local and private IP addresses, including IPv6 support.

- Updated translations

- More reliable full screen detection on Windows with reduced chance of crashes.

- Fixed a bug that could set the app to the wrong language on startup.

- Search via acronyms has been fixed to properly work with results that contain numbers.

## Contributions
We would like to directly mention and thank the following people (in alphabetical order) for their contribution and support in this release.

@DavidGBrett, @dedonnodev, @Jack251970, @SparkUiX, @taooceros, @VictoriousRaptor and everyone who has joined discussions, added translations, created plugins, reviewed pull requests, put through their ideas or reported bugs.

A big thank you to @JakobOstgren for sponsoring us! ❤️

shotcut.changelog:
## What's Changed

See a  [nicely formatted page](https://www.shotcut.org/blog/new-release-26.9.27/) on the web site.

- Fixed security flaws in upgrade and Whisper downloads (failed HTTPS was retried over HTTP, certificate errors could be ignored, and a downloaded file could be used without a trusted digest).
- Fixed **Mask: Draw (Glaxnimate)** filter, **Operation > Subtract** for 8-bit processing mode (broke in version 25.12).
- Fixed using **Size, Position & Rotate** with **Mask: Apply** filters (broke in version 25.12).
- Improved audio quality by removing a conversion to 16-bit integer and keeping the pipeline in 32-bit float.
- Fixed LV2 external audio plugins not loading on Windows (unless `LV2_PATH` environment var set explicitly).
- Fixed VA-API HEVC hardware encoder on Linux.
- Fixed **Show in Folder** not working with non-ASCII characters on Linux.
- Fixed **Import Subtitles from File** not working on Windows.
- Fixed **Subtitles** view shows incorrect duration (broke in version 26.8).
- Fixed moving **Timeline** clip next to another with snap while zoomed out may insert 1 blank frame.
- Fixed copy and pasting a **Timeline** transition corrupt audio in the pasted transition.
- Fixed window title bar missing on Linux with **Settings > Display Method > Vulkan**.
- Fixed marker unexpectedly deleted when moving a clip to the left with **Ripple Markers** on.
- Fixed keyframes on **Timeline > Split** after a transition.
- Fixed **Export** job may report failure even though file was completed successfully.
- Fixed some buffer overflow security issues in PGM/wipe reading in MLT and **Set Equirectangular** in Shotcut.
- Fixed projects deleted from disk still appear in **Projects**.
- Fixed `Ctrl+Up` and `Ctrl+Down` cannot change current track when **Timeline** loses focus.
- Fixed **Player > External Monitor > DeckLink** (and related such as UltraStudio) HDMI/SDI may deadlock. 
- Fixed MLT XML nested clip's length (duration) not updated, now updates when selected but needs manual trim to increase clip.
- Fixed redundant context menu on text edit controls in filters on Windows (broke in v26.8).
- Fixed open project on a mounted CIFS/SMB share on Linux kernel 7.1 and above.
- Fixed possible crash when trying to add subtitle item in the last half second of the timeline.
- Hardened MP4 parsing in **Set Equirectangular** in **Properties** and export job context menu.
- Changed **Settings > Leave Safe Mode** to an always-present **Allow External Plugins** checkbox that defaults to off.
  This helps prevent the problem that some VST2 plugins on Windows and macOS are causing startup and shutdown (including export) problems.
- Detect a stuck application startup to automatically disable external plugins.
- Added **Automatic Audio Ducking** for audio to timeline track **Properties**.
- Changed **Adjust Clip Gain** for timeline clips to require `Ctrl+Alt` (`option+command` on macOS) to drag.
  This makes it safe from inadvertent changes while selecting and dragging clips. So, now that setting
  defaults on again. Also, a tooltip was added to the clip's audio line. 
- Added volume control and audio level meter/indicator to **Timeline** track headers.
  This effectively makes the track header column a mixing console without needing to clutter the UI with a new panel.
  The gain filter this adds to the track is keyframable.
- Added **Timeline > Generate > Adjustment Clip**. This is a dummy video clip that contributes no video.
  Instead, its filters apply to the composite of all video tracks below it.
- Added `application.triggerAction(name)`, `multitrack.clipStart()`, and `timeline.split()` functions for scripts.
- Added a context menu with **Copy** to **Missing Files** dialog and **View > Resources**.
- Improved the performance of the **Timeline**: moving clips to another track, zooming, undo for many operations (except for ripple move/trim).
- Improved the appearance of the user interface to be more modern with rounded corners in many places.
- New logo
- Upgraded FFmpeg to version 9.0

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/mltframework/shotcut/compare/v26.8.1...v26.9.27

With this release, Terminal 1.25 is being rolled out to General Availability; see [the prior version](https://github.com/microsoft/terminal/releases/tag/v1.25.2733.0) for overall release notes.

## Changes

* (1.26 backport) conhost: we now always use the "cls" detector to prevent screen clearing from committing the entire (virtualized) text buffer (#19957)

## Bug Fixes
 
### Accessibility
 
* The "delete" confirmation flyouts will no longer be truncated on higher Text Scaling settings (#20868)
 
### Terminal Emulation

* The Kitty Keyboard Protocol mode will now be maintained properly across main/alternate screen buffer switches (#20768)
* `LNM` line feed mode will no longer be mishandled when it is toggled before and after a newline in the same packet (#20863)
* Applications can no longer set window titles longer than 1000 characters (like xterm) (#20839)
* Applications which scroll the screen buffer will once again be translated properly (such as `vi` from 1996) (#20774)
* Clicking on a URL while an application is reading mouse reports will no longer generate a spurious mouse release event (#20756) (thanks @OmarMashal0!) (edit: er, I (@DHowett) cannot confirm that this is actually fixed)
* Injected keyboard input will no longer come out with unexpected vkey values such as `0xFFFF` (#20800) (thanks @shrikargs7-cloud!)
* Terminal once again sends the `ENHANCED_KEY` state to console applications for Alt and F7 (#20619) (thanks @TheJesper!)
 
### Others

* `useAcrylicInTabRow` users rejoice! We've fixed one of the major sources of flickering in the title bar (#20881)
* `file:` URIs containing Unicode characters will no longer send us into a wild tailspin (#20809)
* Terminal will no longer load up a US keyboard on you (whoops) (#20769)
* Writing a non-numeric value in the command history pop-up will no longer act unexpectedly (#20779)

# Motrix 2.4.1

English | [简体中文](https://github.com/agalwood/Motrix/blob/main/docs/release-notes/2.4.1.zh-CN.md)

## Changes since 2.4.0

- Bundle **aria2 1.37.0-motrix.24**. On Windows, the engine tries the remaining resolved addresses for a host after a connection fails. It reports a network error if all candidates fail. Existing DNS and IPv6 defaults are preserved.
- Upgrade to **i18next 27.0.1** and **react-i18next 18.0.1**. The desktop app, Web UI and Server CLI continue to fall back to `en-US` for missing translations.
- Refresh the form validation, IP database, proxy and WebSocket dependencies, along with the Vite build tools and the jsdom test environment.

## Upgrade compatibility

**Back up your profile and download files before upgrading.** The bundled engine
uses SQLite **schema 6**. When upgrading an older engine database, retain its
complete pre-upgrade backup; older engines cannot open schema 6. Stop all engines
before restoring a verified backup to a separate path for a downgrade. Do not
reset or delete the upgraded database as a substitute for recovery.

Users migrating from Motrix v1 should follow the
[migration guide](https://github.com/agalwood/Motrix/blob/v2.4.1/docs/legacy-migration.md)
and retain the original profile and engine database backups.

## Downloads and updates

Desktop packages support macOS 13 or later, Windows 10 or later, and Linux, with
native x64 and ARM64 builds. No 32-bit desktop packages are provided. Official
macOS packages require signing and notarization. Windows NSIS installers and ZIP
archives are unsigned and may trigger SmartScreen; use official Release downloads.

Stable publication updates both `latest*.yml` and `beta*.yml` feeds to 2.4.1.
Flatpak bundles and Native Host companions remain separate downloads. Snap
availability requires verified Store publication to edge and promotion of the
same amd64/arm64 revisions through candidate to stable.

Server images use `docker.io/motrixapp/motrix-server:2.4.1` and
`ghcr.io/agalwood/motrix-server:2.4.1`. After public multi-platform runtime
verification, `2.4`, `2`, `stable`, and `latest` advance to the same verified digest.
See the [Docker Server guide](https://github.com/agalwood/Motrix/blob/v2.4.1/docs/docker-server.md).

[Full changelog](https://github.com/agalwood/Motrix/compare/v2.4.0...v2.4.1)

The Windows installer package may require an Internet connection to download the latest Microsoft Visual C++ Runtime if your PC does not already have it installed. If you do not have Internet access during installation, you can pre-install the runtime from [Microsoft's website](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/topic/the-latest-supported-visual-c-downloads-2647da03-1eea-4433-9aff-95f26a218cc0) or use the portable version.

To update an existing installation, simply run the latest installer (for Windows) or replace the old app in your Applications folder (for Mac). For the portable Windows version, extract the ZIP into a new folder and copy the `Moonlight Game Streaming Project` folder from the older version to preserve your settings and paired hosts.

**Important note for Windows Portable upgrades from v6.1.0 or earlier:** If you extracted the portable Windows v6.2.0 ZIP file into the same folder as an earlier version of Moonlight, you must delete `qopensslbackend.dll` file in the `tls` folder or Moonlight will crash on startup.

To install on Steam Link hardware, extract the ZIP file to the root of a FAT32 flash drive, insert it into your Steam Link, then restart the Steam Link. Moonlight can run alongside official Steam Link streaming and other Steam Link apps.

**Behavior changes:**
- The default renderer on macOS is now libplacebo (using MoltenVK). You can change renderers on macOS in the Advanced Settings.
- Most video renderers now use full range color instead of limited range
- The cursor is now also locked to the video area in single display borderless windowed scenarios. This was previously only done in true full-screen mode.
- The cursor is no longer captured by default in windowed mode. Clicking on the streaming window or pressing Ctrl+Alt+Shift+Z will capture the cursor.
- Game Mode has been re-enabled on macOS
- The Metal renderer is supported on Macs with a discrete GPU. It was previously only available on Macs with an iGPU.
- HDR metadata is now used for tonemapping on macOS. You may need to tweak your HDR brightness in the OS, particularly for external non-Apple displays.
- CLI output is now displayed in the console on Windows instead of a dialog box
- GPUs on non-x86 Linux platforms are now assumed to be slow by default, which enables a number of optimizations for improved performance. GL_IS_SLOW=0/VULKAN_IS_SLOW=0 can be set at runtime to override this.
- Gamepad motion sensors are disabled on Steam Link hardware to help reduce audio glitching caused by high CPU usage. The moonlight.sh script can be edited to re-enable them.
- The default streaming resolution for new installs is now 1080p instead of 720p.
- Video bitrate no longer resets when adjusting resolution or frame rate if it's already been manually adjusted

**Security:**
- CVE-2026-33546, CVE-2026-33547, and CVE-2026-41210 have been fixed
- These vulnerabilities could allow a malicious host to crash Moonlight when connecting

**New Features:**
- Ctrl+Alt+Shift+K has been added to toggle system keyboard grab
- D3D11 renderer has been updated to enable VRR support on Nvidia GPUs and improve performance by reducing VRAM copies and allowing overlapping decoding and rendering operations
- KMSDRM renderer is rewritten to support atomic modesetting, overlays, VRR, ALLM, software decoding, V-sync off with atomic async flip, and more
- Vulkan rendering is now supported on Linux outside of a desktop environment (KMSDRM)
- AV1 hardware decoding is now supported on macOS (M3 and later)
- AppImages now support using the system libva to prevent hardware decoding failure on distros with newer libva versions
- Added support for DualSense adaptive triggers (requires a compatible host)
- Gamepads with a second trackpad can now be passed to the host (requires host support)
- Client identifiers are now provided to the host to allow client-specific session management
- Added an option to disable pre-launch warnings

A lot of people seem to be unaware of some of the awesome features that have been added to MPC-HC in the past years. Here is a list of useful options and features that everyone should know about:
<details><summary><ins>Click to expand</ins></summary>

This requires using either MPC Video Renderer (MPCVR) or [madVR](http://forum.doom9.org/showthread.php?t=146228).
These renderers can be selected here:
Options > Playback > Output
With other video renderers, the colors will be wrong!
MPCVR is included and is the recommended and default renderer for modern systems. MadVR needs to be installed separately. MPCVR also supports Dolby Vision. MadVR does not.
For optimal performance you should change the hardware decoder to D3D11 in LAV Video Decoder settings when using MPCVR on Windows 10/11, because this renderer uses DirectX11.
* The installer of MPC-HC is very basic (and that will not change).
I therefore recommend using [K-Lite Codec Pack](http://codecguide.com/download_kl.htm). That includes MPC-HC and other essential components. It has a very advanced installation that can automatically create file associations, and helps you with easy configuration of important MPC-HC settings, such as preferred subtitle language(s). It also does automatic configuration of renderer and hardware decoding, for best performance and HDR support.
The Standard version should be sufficient for most people. Use Full version of you like to use MadVR.

Options > Player > User Interface
It is also possible to change the height of the seekbar and size of the toolbar buttons.

You can add/remove/re-order the player buttons.
There are also several different toolbar designs to choose from.
* Video preview on the seekbar
Options > Player > User Interface > Hover type
* Ability to search for subtitles
Press D for manual search.
Or enable automatic search in: Options > Subtitles > Misc 
* Adjust playback speed
Menu > Play > Playback rate
The buttons in the player that control playback rate take a 2x step by default. This can be customized to smaller values (like 10%):
Options > Playback > Speed step
If you have 1000 IQ you can even do smart stuff like setting playback rate change to mouse right-click + scrollwheel:
Options > Player > Mouse
Adjusting playback speed works best with MPC Audio Renderer or SaneAR. These audio renderers have automatic pitch correction, while DirectSound does not.
Options > Playback > Output > Audio Renderer
* MPC-HC can remember recently played files and also their playback position, so you can resume playback from when you left
Options > Player > History
* You can quickly seek through a video with Ctrl + Mouse Scrollwheel.
* You can jump to next/previous file in a folder by pressing PageUp/PageDown.
* You can right-click on the framestep button to step backwards. Some other buttons also have right-click actions, such as closing file by right-clicking stop.
* You can perform automatic actions at end of file. For example to go to next file or close player.
Options > Playback > After Playback (permanent setting)
Menu > Play > After Playback (for current file only)
* A-B repeat
You can loop a segment of a video. Press [ and ] to set start and stop markers.
* You can rotate/flip/mirror/stretch/zoom the video
Menu > View > Pan&Scan
This is also easily done with hotkeys (see below).
* There are lots of keyboard hotkeys and mouse actions to control the player. They can be customized as well.
Options > Player > Keys
Tip: there is a search box above the table.
* You can hide GUI elements even in windowed mode

That hides most GUI elements during playback. To show them simply move your mouse to bottom of window.
You can even hide everything except the video by pressing `1` (restore normal view with `3`). 
* You can seek inside the playlist by simply typing text (when playlist window has the mouse focus).
* MPC-HC also supports Blu-ray playback.

Then you can open website URLs in the player: Menu > File > Open File/URL

These are the offline installers, portable ZIPs, and deployment MSIs for Paint.NET. The web installer is also provided, which will download and run the correct installer for any supported CPU and OS.

**Release notes:** https://forums.paint.net/topic/134628-paintnet-52-is-now-available

**System Requirements**
- Windows 11, or Windows 10 v21H2, or Windows Server 2022
- 64-bit CPU (Intel/AMD x64 with AVX2, or ARM64) with at least 4 cores
- GPU with support for Direct3D 11
- SSD
- _Optional:_ A display that supports High Dynamic Range (HDR) or Wide Color Gamut (WCG)
- _Optional:_ A pen or drawing tablet that supports Windows Ink

**Experimental**
- Wine🍷 support (e.g. Linux and Mac) is available in a separate package at https://github.com/paintdotnet/Paint.NET-on-WINE

**Notes about supported hardware:**
- Examples of CPUs with AVX2 include:
  - Intel Core 4th generation (Haswell, 2013) or newer
  - AMD Ryzen 1st generation (2017) or newer.
- For HDR and WCG displays, Paint.NET will be able to make use of the display's full color gamut and Windows will manage color accuracy and consistency. Images will not be clamped to sRGB's color gamut.
- For SDR displays, Paint.NET will operate in sRGB mode which means images will be clamped to sRGB's color gamut. This ensures consistent color reproduction, but color accuracy depends on the display itself being configured for sRGB as well.

**Notes about unsupported hardware:**
- Intel/AMD CPUs without AVX2 will still work but will be slower. Our testing and optimization efforts no longer include Intel/AMD CPUs without AVX2. **_However_, if your CPU does not support SSE4.2 then the app will not work at all.**
- CPUs with less than 4 cores should still work but will be slower.
- An HDD will work but will have slow performance and it is not supported. Our testing and optimization efforts no longer include HDDs.
- GPUs that do not support Direct3D 11 cannot be used, relegating those tasks to the CPU. Performance will be slower, and some effects may take an excruciatingly long time to render.

_(Friendly hint: If you don't know what an MSI is, then it's almost certainly not the download you want. Just grab the "anycpu" installer if you're not sure which one to use.)_

_The "source code" ZIP does not contain any actual files or source code, it is just included automatically as part of GitHub's "releases" functionality._

Logseq 2.0.2 Beta brings smoother editing, faster startup, and more reliable everyday workflows to the DB version.

[Join the iOS TestFlight beta](https://testflight.apple.com/join/eBcJ9Hpc), 2.0.2 is currently under App Store review.

Web app: https://app.logseq.com/

## Features

- Gallery cards can now use URL properties as covers.
- Added a "Clear heading" slash command.
- Improved video embeds, with resizable desktop players and clickable YouTube timestamps.

## Thanks

- **Special thanks to our community PR contributors!** Your fixes, performance improvements, translations, and careful reviews helped make this beta better. Contributors include [@yuxi-liu-wired](https://github.com/yuxi-liu-wired), [@ChipNowacek](https://github.com/ChipNowacek), [@Mancn-Xu](https://github.com/Mancn-Xu), [@hahaArthur17](https://github.com/hahaArthur17), [@maksym-dilanian](https://github.com/maksym-dilanian), [@qwist1233-cpu](https://github.com/qwist1233-cpu), and many others.
- **A heartfelt thank-you to everyone testing the DB beta.** Your bug reports, reproduction steps, feedback, and retesting of fixes have been invaluable. Thank you for helping us improve Logseq with your real-world graphs and workflows!

## Fixed issues

Ordered by impact on data integrity, reliability, and everyday workflows.

1. **Preserve unsaved edits:** Save pending text before following page or block references, switching blocks, or setting Deadline/Scheduled. Pasting multiple blocks no longer lets a stale editor buffer erase the first pasted title.
2. **Restore deleted content with undo/redo:** Restore deleted blocks and pages that reference each other, along with property schemas and values. Undoing block moves now preserves their original order and nested structure.
3. **Keep block trees intact when copying or moving:** Selecting an ancestor together with its descendants no longer pulls grandchildren out of their subtree. Copy/paste preserves the original child blocks, and embed actions operate on the embed rather than its source.
4. **Keep graph and asset downloads running:** One failed asset download no longer stops the remaining asset queue or fails the graph download. Sync also keeps property-value replacements together instead of splitting them across requests.
5. **Fix Windows installation:** Fix the NSIS installer crash affecting Windows 11 24H2 and newer, so the desktop app can be installed normally.
6. **Improve file-to-DB import fidelity:** Preserve headings, icons, journal timestamps, and PDF annotation identities/order. Asset links in property values are converted into asset references, and same-title classes and properties remain distinct.
7. **Correct scheduled dates and repeating tasks:** Deadline/Scheduled repeats now advance in the local calendar. Monthly repeats no longer drift permanently after a shorter month; date filters use local days, and clearing dates removes stale journal references.
8. **Prevent query errors from crashing the graph:** Incomplete query syntax, invalid regular expressions, and query-function rendering errors are isolated. Query-builder filters again show property/tag names and include custom Status and Priority choices.
9. **Fix property editing and choice selection:** Selected node values remain visible in property pickers, choice identities resolve consistently, and configuration toggles save the newly selected value. Empty multi-value slots and date values can be cleared without errors.
10. **Restore readable search results and references:** Resolve UUID references in search titles, breadcrumbs, and nested page references. References to deleted nodes remain visible as broken links, and opening search no longer clears its results.
11. **Restore settings and HTML publishing:** Settings can be saved when config.edn is missing or invalid, and the first export.css edit creates the file correctly. HTML exports no longer open as a blank page and honor the configured home page.
12. **Make desktop editing and keyboard input reliable:** Clicks during scrolling now open the editor. A click after Escape or Shift+Up/Down keeps the newly opened editor, and fixes cover international dead-key input and IME confirmation in search.
13. **Fix Android popup and layout issues:** Nested popups reuse the presented native sheet, sheet dismissal avoids re-entry, and the layout respects the status-bar safe area. Mobile cloud-graph download and sync triggers work again.

## Enhancements

- **Faster startup and smoother editing:** Improved desktop startup, journal loading, large-page rendering, table scrolling, and search, with fewer unnecessary updates while typing.
- **Better everyday workflows:** Improved flashcard practice, date and repeating-task handling, international keyboard input, plugin APIs, CLI behavior, and translations.

[Full changelog](https://github.com/logseq/logseq/compare/2.0.1...2.0.2)

git.changelog:
Changes since Git for Windows v2.56.0(4) (October 26th 2026)

This addresses the security issues CVE-2026-111760, CVE-2026-113408, CVE-2026-114466, CVE-2026-114467, CVE-2026-114469 and CVE-2026-105437.

### Security bug fixes

* [CVE-2026-111760](https://github.com/git/git/security/advisories/GHSA-vp2w-7xxj-jvxr):

  Recursive clones are susceptible to Remote Code Execution: an attacker-controlled repository can be crafted in a way that exploits a bug in Git whereby Git can be fooled into overwriting a gitfile (used for submodules) with a symbolic link that then points to a directory with malicious config or hooks. The config or hooks may have attacker-specified code.

* [CVE-2026-113408](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/git/-/work_items/809):

  It is possible for a server to advertise an unborn HEAD that contains path-traversal characters (e.g., `refs/heads/../../../TARGET`). With the files ref backend that can lead to ref-updating actions to write to unwanted files.

* [CVE-2026-114467](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/git/-/work_items/810):

  When Git strips the GPG signatures from a commit message, it only accounts for two signatures. A commit message containing more than two signatures therefore causes a stack memory corruption.

  This can be triggered when using `git merge` with a tag which contains more than two signatures. As such, this makes way for a DoS attack which can potentially also affect forges when such a tag is pushed to a remote and a merge action is initiated.

* [CVE-2026-114469](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/git/-/work_items/811):

  Git rejects patches larger than ~1 GiB, because its patch application code does not work well with large files. That check, however, only considered the size of the patch as it appears in the input, which for binary patches is much smaller than the size of the file the patch describes, as binary patches are compressed and encoded. A binary patch that inflates to a very large size therefore slipped past the check and crashed Git with an out-of-bounds read.

* [CVE-2026-105437](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/git/-/work_items/814):

  When merging, Git computes the size of the buffer holding the merge result in a way that can overflow for very large merges, which can be triggered by a large number of conflicts combined with a large `conflict-marker-size`. The resulting buffer can then be too small, and Git writes past its end (and, before and after that, before its start), corrupting the heap.

* [CVE-2026-114466](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/git/-/work_items/812):

  In response to CVE-2019-1348, `fast-import` disallows the `export-marks` feature by default. The features `rewrite-submodules-to` and `rewrite-submodules-from` as well as the option `export-pack-edges` that were introduced in the meantime also allow reading from arbitrary paths, and are therefore now also disallowed by default.

## Jan v0.8.8: security fixes, llama.cpp 0.7.0, and Trusted Hosts for the local API

A security update to v0.8.7. We recommend updating. Your data and settings carry over; a few behaviours change, listed under **What you might notice**.

### Security

- **Links in chat open in your browser.** Links in model replies, tool results, model cards and release notes now always open in your system browser, never inside Jan's window. Links that aren't web or email links are shown as plain text.
- **The local API server checks where browser requests come from.** A web page can only call it if its origin is trusted: the same machine, Jan itself, or a host you list in **Trusted Hosts**. Requests without a browser origin (SDKs, scripts, curl, Claude Code) work as before.
- **Server-side tool execution stays opt-in for every endpoint.** Requests to the local API run MCP tools only when **Settings > Local API Server** allows server-side tool execution.
- **Paths are checked before Jan reads or writes them.** Thread and assistant ids, and the file operations extensions use, stay inside Jan's data folder.
- **The Claude Code integration writes your shell profile safely.** Values are quoted, unusual variable names are refused, and Jan's lines are kept in one marked block that Reset removes completely without touching your own lines.
- **The agent's file tools no longer follow a link out of their workspace**, and folders such as your home, credentials and startup folders can't be attached as writable.
- **Windows: Jan runs system tools from the Windows system folder**, and sign-in links are opened without going through `cmd`.
- **MCP sign-in only uses web addresses** (`http`/`https`) for its endpoints.

### What you might notice

- **Trusted Hosts for browser-based clients.** A web app on another machine (for example Open WebUI's direct connection) or a browser extension calling Jan's API needs its host added to **Settings > Local API Server > Trusted Hosts**. Entries can include a scheme, so `app://obsidian.md` works for Obsidian plugins (thanks to [@SnowingFox](https://github.com/SnowingFox), [#8608](https://github.com/janhq/jan/issues/8608)). Pages without a normal origin (local files, sandboxed frames) can be allowed by listing `file://` or `null`.
- **The CORS switch now takes effect**, and it starts **on** after updating. In earlier versions it was shown but had no effect.
- **Custom environment variables for Claude Code:** keys that change how programs are found (`PATH`, `PATHEXT`, `SystemRoot`, `ComSpec`, `LD_*`, `DYLD_*`, `JAN_*` and the GPU runtime paths Jan uses) are refused with a message. Other variables, including `NODE_OPTIONS`, save as before.
- **Moving the data folder** to a system folder, your home folder itself or a drive root (for example `D:\`) is refused; choose a folder such as `D:\Jan`.
- **MCP servers whose sign-in endpoints aren't web addresses** now show a sign-in error.

### New

**llama.cpp engine 0.7.0.**

The bundled engine moves from 0.5.0 to 0.7.0 (b11669). New per-model settings: an **MoE expert GPU cache** for mixture-of-experts models, **Probabilistic draft sampling** and **Draft batch size** for speculative decoding. They default to the engine's own defaults, so nothing changes unless you set them. Saved prompt caches from the previous engine are discarded once and rebuilt. ([#9399](https://github.com/janhq/jan/pull/9399))

### Fixes

**Local models failed to load on Windows when the user name had non-English characters** (for example Cyrillic). ([#9418](https://github.com/janhq/jan/pull/9418))

**With an HTTP proxy configured, documents with "Use embeddings" failed**, because Jan's requests to its own engine went through the proxy. They now go direct; remote providers still use the proxy. ([#9353](https://github.com/janhq/jan/pull/9353))

**An attachment was sent again on every turn**, adding a copy per message and defeating the prompt cache. It's now included once per request. Thanks to [@yaodong-shen](https://github.com/yaodong-shen). ([#9358](https://github.com/janhq/jan/pull/9358))

**With Shell turned off, a model that called the shell ended its reply.** It now gets "Shell is turned off" and the reply continues. ([#9319](https://github.com/janhq/jan/issues/9319))

**macOS: quitting Jan left the MLX server running** with its model in memory. It's stopped on quit, and one left by an earlier Jan is stopped at startup; an MLX server you started yourself is left alone. ([#9355](https://github.com/janhq/jan/pull/9355))

### Thanks

Fixes in this release include work from [@greatjourney589](https://github.com/greatjourney589) ([#8068](https://github.com/janhq/jan/pull/8068)), [@SnowingFox](https://github.com/SnowingFox) ([#8627](https://github.com/janhq/jan/pull/8627)) and [@orenyomtov](https://github.com/orenyomtov).

### Known issues

- **Auto compact** needs **Max Context Tokens** set for remote models; Jan does not detect a remote model's context window yet ([#9317](https://github.com/janhq/jan/issues/9317)).
- Local models do not run on Intel Macs, as in v0.8.5.
